summary: Service.stopping now calls router.closeWatches() after marking the service not ready, ending all in-flight watch streams. Without this, the HTTP server's Shutdown would wait on watches that never go idle. Clients are expected to re-watch against another replica.
headline: Service stop now terminates all active watch streams
reason: Adds a call in the shutdown path that forcibly ends long-lived client connections, which is a runtime lifecycle and concurrency behavior change.
focus: closeWatches is safe to call when no watches exist, when called twice, and concurrently with reconcile
Order relative to SetNotReady, so new watches are not accepted after closeWatches runs
Watches opened after stopping begins are also ended or rejected
Clients end cleanly (complete response, not aborted connection) so they re-watch
